scope: Independent rendered design and sampled-motion review of the final two 21-second App Store previews and their 15-second posters. All review is local; no upload or account operation performed. This does not certify app-wide behavior, randomness, accessibility, or App Store acceptance.
evidenceMethod: Decoded both videos independently at 2 frames/second; inspected overview and consecutive draw-phase galleries, plus original-resolution spinning, winner, history/reset, repaired final phone reset at 19 and 20.5 seconds, and both 15-second posters. Entire final files were decoded for errors and blackdetect; ffprobe and volume analysis were run. This is frame/timeline inspection, not a claim of human real-time playback.

categoryEvidence.audienceResonance: The sequence demonstrates list setup, changing wheel, an identifiable celebratory winner, and a names-preserving reset for a host. The long winner hold suits a reveal but leaves less time for operating details.
categoryEvidence.categoryRecognition: Numbered pool, spinning vertical selector, result medal, and reset confirmation establish random group selection. The opening tablet input view alone is less distinctive until motion begins.
categoryEvidence.productSpecificity: Ethan #8 and Owen #16, active counts, no-repeat state, numbered history, and NameSnap's own celebration artwork prevent this from reading as a generic animation. The input roster is intentionally synthetic.
categoryEvidence.primaryTaskClarity: Each file moves from populated input to a visible SPINNING state and winner. No finger indicator is shown, and the input/add step is introduced through an edit rather than an uninterrupted tutorial.
categoryEvidence.visualHierarchy: Winners dominate their screens and the final reset actions remain complete. iPad's full layout leaves its wheel and dialog relatively small in gallery thumbnails.
categoryEvidence.compositionDiversity: Input, operational wheel, full-screen celebration, and centered confirmation create distinct stages. The opening and reset are static holds, and both devices follow the same appropriate demonstration structure.
categoryEvidence.contentRealism: Both clips show a real changing draw state and coherent winners. Phone resolves to Ethan Nguyen #8 and tablet to Owen Lewis #16; each post-winner scene retains that history and 15 TOTAL from an initial 16.
categoryEvidence.domainArtifactFidelity: The actual vertical picker and real app panels are shown without a fabricated radial wheel or marketing device shell. Input action itself is not shown as a live edit.
categoryEvidence.crossScreenContinuity: Phone #8 Ethan persists from reveal into result/history with 15 active; iPad #16 Owen does likewise. Reset is still a confirmation, so 15 before confirmation is correct. Input and reset are separately captured segments, not one wholly uncut recording.
categoryEvidence.platformFidelity: Phone live/reset detail segments omit the problematic status strip through an aspect-preserving top crop with pale padding; modal X, dialog actions, toolbar, and home indicator remain whole. Tablet retains its native full canvas. The real fixed toolbar remains bright behind dimmed reset content.
categoryEvidence.spatialEconomy: Phone uses most of the frame. Tablet opening and celebration retain generous native whitespace, and the winner has a long held presentation. This is readable but less economical than the tighter phone composition.
categoryEvidence.typography: Names, result IDs, actions, and 15 TOTAL badges are readable at original resolution. Tablet operational metadata and celebration variation labels are small in thumbnails; wheel neighbors intentionally fade.
categoryEvidence.accessibility: Numbered results, text labels, checkmarks, and complete Cancel/Reset actions provide non-color cues. Confetti and motion are visible; reduced-motion behavior and assistive access are not tested. The intentionally silent export communicates its story visually.
categoryEvidence.interactionCredibility: Consecutive frames show names changing while SPINNING is disabled, followed by a numbered winner and matching history. This resolves the earlier static-state demonstration weakness. The montage does not prove the paste gesture, random distribution, or execution of the final reset.
categoryEvidence.stateCompleteness: The listing preview covers prepared input, spinning, success, post-winner history/count, and destructive confirmation. It does not show empty/error/exhausted state or completed reset, which remain outside this short preview's claims.
categoryEvidence.distinctiveness: Different authentic celebrations—drummer for Ethan and DJ artwork for Owen—show NameSnap's numbered, playful reveal. The full-screen celebration occupies a large fraction of the runtime.
categoryEvidence.appStorePlausibility: Clean current-app footage, readable posters, coherent results, and bounded edits form a credible listing preview. There are no fake controls or external promotional scenes. The silent track and long holds are a modest presentation tradeoff.
categoryEvidence.implementationReadiness: The render script defines sources, trims, crop, padding, encodes, and poster time; final decoded specifications and SHA-256 hashes identify reviewed files. Source capture timing remains dependent on the recorded session.
categoryEvidence.componentSemantics: Final result, medal number, history item, no-repeat state, and 16-to-15 count change agree on both devices. Intermediate name banners differ from the moving wheel during animation; these are transient spinning states, not a second finalized result.
categoryEvidence.materialFit: Warm actions, violet outlines, light panels, and animated confetti fit playful group picking while leaving current names legible. Heavy shadows and fades remain inherited app styling.

blurTest.evidence: The sequence visibly changes from list to operational selector to celebratory result and confirmation; the dominant objects remain recognizable even when text details are small.

silhouetteTest.evidence: Full roster, vertical wheel, large winner, and modal confirmation have different structures. Both device files follow the same product journey; no unrelated-product composition is copied.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: By the early draw phase, the viewer sees the numbered picker visibly SPINNING, followed soon by an unmistakable winner. The opening list and app name establish context.

realityTest.evidence: The capture contains genuine changing wheel states and coherent synthetic contestant data. Final Ethan #8 / Owen #16 histories each correspond to 15 remaining. No fabricated UI is composited.

componentSemanticTest.evidence: Original-scale checks cover spinning label, wheel rows, winner medal/name, recent winner, count, and reset dialog. Complete labels and values agree after settlement; reset confirms the effects rather than pretending they already happened.

journeyTest.evidence: Final phone winner #8 Ethan and tablet winner #16 Owen persist into their corresponding history/count/reset segments. The earlier montage's return to 16 after a no-repeat winner is eliminated. The add action and reset confirmation execution are not claimed as observed.

platformTest.evidence: Final phone ending at 19s and 20.5s no longer contains prior-card fragments overlapping status icons. All modal and toolbar controls stay intact; iPad has no comparable clipping. Pale padding preserves detail-frame aspect.

buyerValueTest.evidence: The viewer receives an actual moving selection and numbered reveal rather than only fixture stills. Current app controls and the final confirmation make the product's use concrete.

implementationTest.evidence: The checked render script and independently recorded final specs/hashes reproduce the three-segment pipeline, dimensions, crop/padding, 21-second encoding and 15-second poster extraction.

categoryReferenceTest.evidence: Compared with the already-inspected current Apple references for Tiny Decisions, Spin The Wheel, and Decide Now: immediate draw/result grammar is retained, with NameSnap's own vertical picker, IDs, and celebration. No radial-wheel cliché, copied reference imagery, or store-frame chrome leaks into the app footage.

screenFindings.screen: Both videos, initial and draw phase
screenFindings.finding: The former six-second ready-wheel hold has been replaced by actual changing SPINNING states and a continuous recorded reveal. Opening setup remains an editorial introduction, not a paste demonstration.
Ethan Nguyen #8 agrees across the medal, winner description, result banner, and history. The active count becomes15.
Owen Lewis #16 agrees across medal, winner description, result banner, and history. The active count becomes15. Confetti has no opaque black rectangle.

Initial review found a previous card overlapping status icons at the top. Final crop at 19s and 20.5s removes that strip while preserving Draw Setup, reset explanation/actions, Ethan history, 15 TOTAL, toolbar, and home indicator.
Final actual winners are shown at full original size with complete close and continuation controls. No incorrect old Ava fixture remains in these reviewed posters.
Winner holds are long and iPad native layouts leave generous whitespace. Silent audio omits the app's music experience. These are tradeoffs, not misleading UI or missing visible controls.

technicalEvidence.video: 630 frames each; H.264 High, yuv420p, 30 fps
technicalEvidence.audio: AAC stereo 48 kHz; mean and peak decoded volume -91.0dB, consistent with intentional silence
technicalEvidence.decode: Both final files decode with exit 0; blackdetect produced no events at minimum 0.1 second and pixel threshold 0.10

unverified: App Store processing/acceptance and uploaded poster selection
Human real-time playback and subjective audio experience (the files are intentionally silent)
Runtime VoiceOver, dynamic type, focus, reduced motion, or modal hit testing
Final reset execution and preservation after its confirmation
Legacy Poster-5s PNG files; only current Poster-15s files are in this verdict
verdict: PASS, 93.7/100, for the final two 21-second previews and their 15-second posters within this local rendered/frame-timeline review. The real-draw and state-continuity repairs are verified, and no critical visible defect remains after the phone ending crop. Upload/release and broader app behavior require their separate checks.
